occasions.moment: the 4pm dip at a desk — hungry, flagging, two hours from dinner
occasions.competes_with: biscuits from the office jar, a chocolate bar, samosa/vada from the canteen, chai, a banana, or skipping it entirely
occasions.decided_by: speed, taste, what is within arm's reach, mild guilt
occasions.channel: office pantry, vending machine, the desk drawer stocked on Blinkit

occasions.moment: 11pm, scrolling in bed, wants something sweet
occasions.competes_with: chocolate, ice cream, leftover mithai, biscuits, nothing
occasions.decided_by: craving, what is in the fridge, 10-minute delivery
occasions.channel: Blinkit / Zepto / Instamart, the kitchen cupboard

occasions.moment: straight after the gym, 45 minutes before a proper meal
occasions.competes_with: a whey shake, eggs, a banana, dal-chawal at home, nothing
occasions.decided_by: protein per serving, habit, what the trainer said
occasions.channel: gym counter, HealthKart, Amazon, the gym bag

occasions.moment: leaving the house late, will not sit down to eat
occasions.competes_with: toast, poha, cereal, a bought sandwich, coffee alone, skipping
occasions.decided_by: one hand, no crumbs, keeps until 11am
occasions.channel: kitchen counter, the metro station kiosk, monthly grocery order

occasions.moment: a weekend or a bad day — wants a treat but not to feel bad about it
occasions.competes_with: dark chocolate, a 'healthy' dessert, regular chocolate anyway, fruit
occasions.decided_by: permission — whether it reads as a treat or as a compromise
occasions.channel: quick commerce, the supermarket aisle, a cafe

occasions.moment: airport, long drive, or a two-hour commute with no real meal in sight
occasions.competes_with: airport sandwich, chips, nuts, a Snickers at the counter, nothing
occasions.decided_by: portability, shelf life, what the counter is selling
occasions.channel: airport store, highway stop, petrol pump, packed from home

occasions.moment: a standing daily habit someone has decided to keep
occasions.competes_with: a powder, gummies, a multivitamin, real food, nothing
occasions.decided_by: routine, whether it is working, cost per day
occasions.channel: Amazon subscribe, HealthKart, the pharmacy, D2C

occasions.moment: the monthly or weekly shop — buying for other people as well as themselves
occasions.competes_with: biscuit packs, namkeen, cereal, whatever the kids will eat
occasions.decided_by: price per unit, family acceptance, keeps in the cupboard

everyday_alternatives: Cadbury Dairy Milk — ₹10 to ₹100 depending on size; the default sweet thing
Snickers — ~₹40 for 50g; the 'it's basically food' bar at the counter
Britannia Good Day, Marie Gold, 50-50, Bourbon — ₹10-₹40 biscuit packs
Parle-G — ₹5-₹10; the floor of the category
Sunfeast Dark Fantasy — ~₹30; the indulgent biscuit
Lay's / Kurkure / Bingo — ₹20 chips and namkeen
Haldiram's namkeen — ₹20-₹50 packs, and the household tin
Amul / Kwality Walls ice cream — ₹40-₹80 for the late-night version
canteen samosa, vada pav, or chai — ₹10-₹25, hot and immediate
a banana or an apple from the fruit cart — ₹10-₹20
leftover mithai in the fridge after any festival
nothing at all — waiting it out until the next meal

raw.label: loyalist_kitkat_break_ritual
raw.l1_context: Fell into the same four o'clock break years ago with whoever else was on shift; the wrapper and the tea arrived together and never changed.
raw.l2_category: Buys a single finger bar four or five afternoons a week at the shop by the gate, ₹20-ish, always the same brand, never online.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows the bar has got thinner over the years and says so. Does NOT know what whey concentrate is or that protein bars are sold in boxes. Does NOT read ingredient lists or sugar order.
raw.l4_stance: Wants the same taste and the same small coin every day. Rejects being told his break is a health decision; refuses anything he has to order in advance.
raw.l5_behavior: Was offered a colleague's ₹80 protein bar last month, ate half, bought his usual finger bar at the gate the same evening.

raw.label: switcher_canteen_samosa_swap
raw.l1_context: Started rotating what he grabs at four because the canteen fry got heavy and he was falling asleep in the 5pm stand-up.
raw.l2_category: Some weeks a wafer bar, some weeks a namkeen pack, occasionally a bar off a ten-minute app; ₹20 to ₹80, no fixed brand.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows one bar sits heavy and one leaves him hungry by six. Does NOT know which brands are actually owned by whom. Does NOT know or believe what 20g of protein does for him.
raw.l4_stance: Wants whichever thing gets him to dinner without a slump. Rejects loyalty pitches and rejects anything sold only as a box of eight.
raw.l5_behavior: Ordered a RiteBite Roots bar on Zepto to the office one Tuesday, went back to the canteen vada the next day.

raw.label: upgrader_desk_drawer_stock
raw.l1_context: A cholesterol line on last year's company health check made him clear the biscuit habit out of the desk drawer and put something else there.
raw.l2_category: Keeps a box in the drawer, reorders every five or six weeks off the brand's own site; around ₹100 a bar and he has stopped flinching at it.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows dates-sweetened bars sit differently than the caramel ones. Does NOT know whether the printed protein number is verified. Does NOT know what creatine or maltodextrin are.
raw.l4_stance: Wants a snack he does not have to negotiate with at four. Rejects gym-bro tubs and rejects the office jar entirely — that is everyone's food, not his.
raw.l5_behavior: Reordered the box of eight Whole Truth bars after the last one ran out mid-month and he ended up at the canteen.

raw.l1_context: Sees the bars in reels and in a senior's bag and wants that to be his four o'clock too; has not once actually bought one.
raw.l2_category: Four o'clock is currently a ₹10 biscuit pack or the free canteen chai; adds bars to a marketplace cart and does not check out.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows the names from ads and from what people at work carry. Does NOT know what any of them taste like. Does NOT know a box is the usual unit, and expects to find singles at the kirana.
raw.l4_stance: Wants to be the man with the good snack in his bag. Rejects the idea that biscuits are fine, but also refuses to spend a whole box's money on a guess.
raw.l5_behavior: Kept a Yogabar variety pack in an Amazon cart for three weeks, then bought a Good Day pack at the corner shop instead.

raw.label: skeptic_protein_on_everything
raw.l1_context: Bought into the bars for a while, then the news about protein numbers being wrong on packs went round his group and he stopped cold.

raw.l5_behavior: Stopped a wafer-box reorder halfway through and started carrying roasted chana from the weekly market instead.
